First Revision)
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 3 1 January 1981, after the draft finalized by the Physical Methods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1968 to cover yarns only. It has been revised to make it applicable to wool tops and fabrics and also to include the use of bnezene-methanol mixture for extraction of the Also the procedure has been modified to calculate the correct material. invoice weight on the basis of the oven dry weight of the specimen. 0.3 This standard has been prepared to eliminate unnecessary and undesirable variations in testing procedure for the determination of correct invoice weight ( obtained by adding appropriate commercial moisture regain to oven dry weight of the material ) of all wool yarns and fabrics. 0.4 To familiarize the industry with International System of Units ( SI Units ), the basic SI Units as well as the recommended SI Units for use in the textile industry are given in Appendix A. 0.4.1 Standards of SI Units. of Weights'and Measures Act 1976 also stipulates use

0.5 In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with th~is standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

shall

2.1 Correct Invoice Weight - The weight of material in a lot calculated from its oven-dry weight by adding to it the appropriate commercial moisture regain. 2.2 Commercial Moisture Regain - An arbitrary value formally adopted as the regain to be used with the oven dry weight -when calculating the correct invoice weight of a shipment or delivery of any specific material. - A general term for a cop, bobbin, tube, pirn, cone, 2.3 Package cheese, hank, bundle of tops, yarn or roll of fabrics indicating that the material is in a form convenient for transport or further processing. 3. SAMPL-ING of wool material tops, yarn or fabric purport3.1 Lot - The quantity ing to be of one definite type~and quality delivered to one buyer against one despatch note. 3.2 Sample drawn in compliance with the specification for the material or as agreed between the concerned parties shall be taken to be representative of the lot. Prepare test sample as given in 3.2.1 to 3.2.3. of about 3.2.1 TO/U - If the wool is in the form of tops, a length one metre shall be removed from each top after discarding and portion. The material taken from different tops shall be thoroughly mixed and a test sample of about 200 g shall he drawn by suitable method. 3.2.2

6. PROCEDURE

8.1 Determine

From the test sample the weight of the consignment(w). of 200 g, take a test specimen weighing about 10 g and put it in a polyethylene bag of known weight, and seal it in theenvironment in which Weigh the bag and find the weight of the the consignment is housed. Take care to see that no change in the moisture test specimen ( Wz ). content of the test specimen takes place during the drawing and weighing of the sample.
*Specification for benzene, reagent grade. tSpccification for methanol ( methyl alcohol ) (Jirrf reuisian ).

5

IS : 4902 - 1981 6.2 Take the test specimen and wrap it in a filter paper. Extract the specimen with the 300 ml of benzene-methanol mixture [ 3 : 2 ( V/V) ] in a soxhlet apparatus for three hours, siphoning the solvent at a minimum rate of 6 extractions per hour. Remove the test specimen and dry it to constant weight in an oven at a~temperature of 105 f 3�C. Determine the weight of the dried extracted specimen ( Wo ). 6.3 Repeat the test with one more test specimen.
